framegen.settings.title: Frame Generation
framegen.message.snapshot_unavailable: FrameGen is not running, nothing to snapshot
framegen.option.enabled.tooltip: Generate in-between frames by reprojecting the last real frames with their depth buffer. Camera motion is shown at your display's refresh rate while the game renders fewer real frames. Toggle in game with F8.
framegen.option.mode.tooltip:
Interpolate (default): blends between the two newest real frames. Smoothest, especially at low frame rates; adds about one real frame of latency.
Extrapolate: predicts the camera forward from the newest frame. No added latency; less smooth at low frame rates and may briefly overshoot when you stop turning.
framegen.option.quality.tooltip: Number of solver iterations per pixel and whether disoccluded areas are filled with background. Higher is more accurate around edges and costs a bit more GPU time on the presentation thread.
framegen.option.multiplier.tooltip: Limits how many real frames the game renders while FrameGen is on. Display rate (recommended): never render more frames than your display shows; FrameGen only fills in when the game drops below it. 1/2 display and lower trade real frames for GPU headroom (only useful if the game stutters). Game limit: use your Max Framerate setting.
framegen.option.output_fps.tooltip: Used when V-Sync is off. With V-Sync on, frames are presented at the display refresh rate.
framegen.option.overscan.tooltip: Renders a little more of the world than fits on screen (this much extra on every side). When you turn fast, generated frames show the real scenery at the screen edges instead of stretched edge pixels. Real frames look exactly the same. Costs GPU time: 8% renders about 35% more pixels. Off when post effects or glowing entities are on screen.
framegen.option.moving_objects.tooltip: Move mobs, players, items, minecarts and boats smoothly in generated frames, instead of only the camera. Walking and turning are smoothed; limb animations still update at the real frame rate.
framegen.option.responsive_camera.toolti: Turn the camera in generated frames with your newest mouse movement, instead of waiting for the next real frame. Turning reacts sooner while the world stays as smooth as before. It uses your real mouse input, not a prediction, so it never overshoots. First person only.
framegen.option.sharp_hud.tooltip: Keep the HUD and your first-person hand out of the reprojection so they never wobble or smear. Disable only if another mod draws HUD elements that look wrong.
framegen.option.extrapolation.tooltip: Extrapolate mode only (no effect with Interpolate): how far ahead of the newest real frame the camera may be predicted, in real frames. Higher keeps motion flowing when frames are late but overshoots more when you stop turning; 0 disables prediction.
framegen.option.low_latency.tooltip: Wait for each presented frame to reach the display before preparing the next one. Lower latency and better pacing on most drivers.
framegen.option.stats.tooltip: Show output / real frame rates in the top left corner.
framegen.option.debug.tooltip: Tint pixels the reprojection could not reconstruct confidently in magenta, and pixels moved with a mob or player in blue.
framegen.status.unsupported_backend: FrameGen inactive: requires the OpenGL graphics API (Video Settings > Graphics API)
framegen.status.failed: FrameGen inactive: could not start (see log)
framegen.stats.redirected: FrameGen paused | %s fps (another mod, e.g. Supersample, is changing the render resolution)
framegen.stats.native: FrameGen native | %s fps (game already keeps up with the display, nothing to generate)
framegen.stats.on: FrameGen %s fps (real %s) | %s | delay %s ms | present %s ms
framegen.stats.on_responsive: FrameGen %s fps (real %s) | %s | delay %s ms, turning %s ms | present %s ms
